prompt: Implement the Visitor pattern over a small expression tree: three visitors -- an evaluator, a fully parenthesised printer, and a depth measurer -- each recursing only through accept. Complete ExpressionVisitors in the starter file, then run the tests.
explanation: The Visitor pattern splits the node types (which are fixed) from the operations over them (which keep being added): each node's accept method calls back into the one visit method that fits it, so no operation ever needs instanceof or a switch. Making the visitor generic in R is what lets the same three-line structure return an Integer for evaluation and a String for printing. Recursion happens by calling child.accept(this) -- the visitor hands itself back down the tree, and the return type threads through automatically.
hints: Each visit method handles one node type and recurses with child.accept(this). For example visitAdd returns add.left().accept(this) combined with add.right().accept(this).
The generic parameter R is the type each visitor produces. Evaluator is an ExprVisitor<Integer>, Printer an ExprVisitor<String>, and the recursion returns that same type at every level.

The static helpers are two lines each: check for null, then expression.accept(new Evaluator()) (or the other visitors). The Printer never needs to know its parent, since every Add and Mul wraps itself in parentheses.
